chapter: Long-running sessions, steering, and CLAUDE.md configuration

questions.question: A consultancy works across 12 client projects. Each developer has personal preferences (editor keybindings), the firm has firm-wide coding standards, and each client project has its own conventions. What's the correct configuration architecture?
options: User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for personal preferences; project CLAUDE.md for firm-wide standards and client conventions; directory-level CLAUDE.md or path-scoped rules for subsystem rules
A single CLAUDE.md at the root of each project containing all configuration levels with clear section headings
User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for everything, using @ path imports to pull in project-specific files from each repo
Put firm-wide standards in the user-level file so they load for every session automatically

questions.question: Why is putting shared, firm-wide standards in a user-level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) file the wrong choice for a multi-developer consultancy?
options: User-level CLAUDE.md applies only to that individual developer and isn't shared via version control, so a colleague cloning the project never receives it
User-level CLAUDE.md always loads after project-level files, so it would be overridden anyway
User-level CLAUDE.md has a hard character limit too small for firm-wide standards
User-level CLAUDE.md can only contain hook configuration, not conventions

questions.question: A team is debugging a complex distributed-system issue: exploring logs, tracing request flows, forming hypotheses, with no changes to the codebase yet. Partway through, they identify a one-line config fix and want to apply it immediately. What's the optimal workflow?
options: Start in plan mode for investigation, then switch to direct execution for the one-line fix once identified
Use direct execution throughout, with detailed upfront instructions describing the investigation process and potential fixes
Use plan mode for the entire session, including the one-line fix, to maintain consistency
Restrict to read-only tools for investigation, then start an entirely new session with write permissions for the fix

questions.question: Why is starting a brand-new session for a one-line fix (after investigating in plan mode within the same session) the wrong move?
options: A new session would lose all the investigation context (log analysis, request tracing, hypothesis formation) that led to identifying the fix
Plan mode can never transition to direct execution within Claude Code
New sessions default to bypassPermissions mode, which is unsafe for a production fix
Starting a new session always regenerates the CLAUDE.md hierarchy from scratch

questions.question: What's the guidance for a hard, non-negotiable rule like 'never push to main'?
options: It belongs in a pre-tool-use hook, not CLAUDE.md — the hook can actually stop the action, CLAUDE.md can only ask
It should be repeated at the top of CLAUDE.md in all caps for emphasis
It should go in the project's README instead of any Claude Code configuration
It doesn't matter where it lives as long as it's mentioned somewhere

questions.question: Which CLAUDE.md rule is written effectively, per the guidance that rules should be specific and checkable?
options: "Put new API routes in src/api/handlers, one per file"
"Follow best practices for API design"
"Don't use default exports" (with no alternative named)
"Be careful with API routes"

questions.question: A Claude Code agent has been working on a feature branch for 45 minutes. Tool results from 40 minutes ago (file reads) are now stale because a colleague pushed changes to those files, and the agent is reasoning from the outdated contents. What is the best recovery strategy?
options: Start a fresh session seeded with a summary of the valuable findings so far, then re-read the changed files from that clean state
Stay in the current session and ask the agent to re-read the changed files — the stale results remain in context regardless
Ignore the staleness since the agent will naturally prioritize newer information over older context
Restart the same session with --continue and hope the model deprioritizes the earlier reads

questions.question: Two Claude Code instances are running in separate git worktrees — Instance A extracting the payment service, Instance B extracting the inventory service — and both need to modify the same shared OrderService.java. How should the team coordinate this?
options: Sequence it: one instance completes its edit and merges first, then the other rebases onto the updated state before making its own changes
Let both instances edit OrderService.java independently and resolve the merge conflict after both are done
Worktrees already isolate each instance's changes, so no coordination is needed for shared files
Have both instances write to separate copies of OrderService.java and merge programmatically at the end
